items.title: Buy a computer tax-free until August 20 — Florida's Back-to-School Sales Tax Holiday covers computers up to $1,500, rules at floridarevenue.com/backtoschool
items.summary: Through Thursday, August 20, Florida's Back-to-School Sales Tax Holiday makes personal computers up to $1,500 tax-free — that includes laptops and desktops, plus accessories like monitors, printers, routers, and ink cartridges. See the full list of what counts at floridarevenue.com/backtoschool, then shop any store — online orders count too.

items.title: Videos too big to email? HandBrake shrinks them for free at handbrake.fr — no subscription, works offline
items.summary: Download HandBrake free from handbrake.fr, open your video, pick the "Fast 1080p30" preset at the top, and hit Start. A video that was too big to attach to an email will fit in a couple of minutes — it works on Windows and Mac, no account, no subscription, and no internet needed once it's installed.

items.title: Windows Update Today: Hackers Were Already Using One of the 400 Holes It Fixes
items.summary: Microsoft released its monthly computer update today — and it's a big one. The free update closes 400 security holes in Windows, including one that a group of hackers was already using to sneak bad programs onto people's computers. Don't put this one off. Open the Start menu, type "check for updates," and let your computer restart when it asks. The update is built into Windows and free from Microsoft. If it ever feels like more than you want to tackle, bring it to us and we'll handle it.

items.title: Got scammed once? Now crooks are coming back for round two — never pay an "upfront fee" to get money back, report it free at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
items.summary: The FTC just issued a new warning about "refund and recovery" scams. Scammers buy lists of people who already lost money to a scam, then call pretending to be a government agency, a law firm, or a consumer group and promise to get the money back — if you first pay a "processing fee" or hand over your bank details. No legitimate organization ever charges you to recover a refund. If it happens, report it free at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

items.title: Microsoft Edge is turning off older add-ons starting this month — swap the classic uBlock Origin for the free uBlock Origin Lite in the Edge Add-ons store, or move to Firefox at firefox.com
items.summary: Microsoft is retiring the older kind of browser add-on in Microsoft Edge starting August 2026, and the classic version of uBlock Origin — one of the most popular free ad blockers — is on the affected list. The fix takes two minutes: open Edge, click the three-dot menu → Extensions → "Get extensions for Microsoft Edge," search "uBlock Origin Lite," and install it free. Or switch to Firefox at firefox.com, where the full uBlock Origin keeps working.

items.title: Don't trust the $5 flea-market flash drive with your photos — buy a genuine SanDisk from sandisk.com or a trusted store
items.summary: Cheap no-name flash drives often lie about their size — a "1TB" stick may really hold only a few gigabytes, and once it's full it quietly overwrites your files. For anything you'd hate to lose — family photos, tax returns, school work — buy a name-brand drive like SanDisk, from sandisk.com or a trusted store like Walmart, Best Buy, or Amazon (sold by SanDisk itself). If the price sounds too good to be true, it's fake.

items.title: Your photos and documents can survive a dead computer — turn on OneDrive backup, built into Windows and free
items.summary: OneDrive is Microsoft's free cloud storage built into Windows. Click the little cloud icon at the bottom-right of your screen (near the clock), then the gear icon → Sync and back up → Manage backup, and turn on Desktop, Documents, and Pictures. From then on, every file in those folders is copied to the cloud automatically — so a dead computer, a spilled drink, or a locked-up drive can't take them. You get 5GB free with a Microsoft account; a Microsoft 365 subscription ups it to a full terabyte.

items.title: Windows 11 August update lets you remove AI components and adds Voice Isolation — get it in Settings > Windows Update
items.summary: The August Windows 11 update adds an AI Components page where Copilot+ PC owners can uninstall the Image Generation model to reclaim storage. It also adds Voice Isolation to Voice Access for better background noise filtering, and extends Windows Hello security to USB fingerprint readers. Get it at Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates.

items.title: Your router's default admin password is public — change it in your router's settings
items.summary: Your router ships with a default admin password that anyone on your network can find. Change it in your router's settings to block automated attacks. Netgear, TP-Link, ASUS, Linksys, Xfinity, and Verizon routers each have a settings page — look for Administration or Security settings. Eero and Google Nest use your account password instead.
